Find $\,\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C)).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 8 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$" :question/worked-solution "The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and no non-pivot column. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has $1$ pivot column and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $3$rd columns). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C))=0+1+2=3.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-f7861d69-8891-56f9-b3bb-6cd69873e91d"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-f7861d69-8891-56f9-b3bb-6cd69873e91d" :answer-field/id #uuid "f7861d69-8891-56f9-b3bb-6cd69873e91d" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-25d9c3ae-c60e-5f23-8b09-bd6f72672565" :answer-field/choices ["answer-62c579bb-353a-5222-8c49-b704acbe87e7" "answer-b08e9ade-c6e5-5b60-ac34-32e78a9a1641" "answer-8d34d79c-138f-5ab3-9fb5-c6f333384a8e" "answer-25d9c3ae-c60e-5f23-8b09-bd6f72672565" "answer-bca9b8c9-b194-53fd-be09-17e6ac4e9236"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-62c579bb-353a-5222-8c49-b704acbe87e7" :answer/id #uuid "62c579bb-353a-5222-8c49-b704acbe87e7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-b08e9ade-c6e5-5b60-ac34-32e78a9a1641" :answer/id #uuid "b08e9ade-c6e5-5b60-ac34-32e78a9a1641" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8d34d79c-138f-5ab3-9fb5-c6f333384a8e" :answer/id #uuid "8d34d79c-138f-5ab3-9fb5-c6f333384a8e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-25d9c3ae-c60e-5f23-8b09-bd6f72672565" :answer/id #uuid "25d9c3ae-c60e-5f23-8b09-bd6f72672565" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-bca9b8c9-b194-53fd-be09-17e6ac4e9236" :answer/id #uuid "bca9b8c9-b194-53fd-be09-17e6ac4e9236" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186319352 :question/problem "Which of the following statements are true?

If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=2.$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-83850766-9b1b-5a37-bf38-12d47d12c4d5" :question/id #uuid "83850766-9b1b-5a37-bf38-12d47d12c4d5" :question/math-academy-id "q-35347" :question/problem "Given $G=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ -2 & 3 & -6 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -6 & -15 & -12 & -16\end{aligned}],\,$ what is $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(G))?$" :question/worked-solution "To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(G))$, we reduce $G$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}G & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ -2 & 3 & -6 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -6 & -15 & -12 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -6 & -15 & -12 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{9}{2} & \frac{11}{4} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $4$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim}(\text{Null}(G))=0.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-2c9771c3-f30b-56b9-83e9-dd0e274a3d9d"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-2c9771c3-f30b-56b9-83e9-dd0e274a3d9d" :answer-field/id #uuid "2c9771c3-f30b-56b9-83e9-dd0e274a3d9d" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-48411ad1-c867-5f45-b8c7-ce3589fd2218" :answer-field/choices ["answer-48411ad1-c867-5f45-b8c7-ce3589fd2218" "answer-01b39024-8f98-5edf-93f7-04a64ee7b6c0" "answer-d56c921a-e74a-5b91-bee7-d13092469fb1" "answer-7ac52ed7-ea31-518a-95fb-dc6ea725ad9d" "answer-69951a24-a52b-5841-8392-9e70e2c63d9d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-48411ad1-c867-5f45-b8c7-ce3589fd2218" :answer/id #uuid "48411ad1-c867-5f45-b8c7-ce3589fd2218" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "0" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-01b39024-8f98-5edf-93f7-04a64ee7b6c0" :answer/id #uuid "01b39024-8f98-5edf-93f7-04a64ee7b6c0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d56c921a-e74a-5b91-bee7-d13092469fb1" :answer/id #uuid "d56c921a-e74a-5b91-bee7-d13092469fb1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-7ac52ed7-ea31-518a-95fb-dc6ea725ad9d" :answer/id #uuid "7ac52ed7-ea31-518a-95fb-dc6ea725ad9d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-69951a24-a52b-5841-8392-9e70e2c63d9d" :answer/id #uuid "69951a24-a52b-5841-8392-9e70e2c63d9d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186125778 :tutorial/content "We already learned that the rank of a matrix $A$ is the number of pivot columns in $A.$ Now, can we obtain any information from the *non-pivot* columns?

The answer is yes! The non-pivot columns help to find the dimension of the null space of a matrix $A,$ and here's how.

Consider the matrix 
![](images/99/991b6f0c69e6341620139db9bfce5303785be21760eb8d630bfee92c57d4bc6a.svg)

The matrix $A$ is already in row echelon form, where the $1$st and the $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd one is a *non-pivot* column. Now, to get the null space of $A,$ we need to find the solution of the system

![](images/1c/1cd56dc26ad4f478c3d7cb14375b8b2e45ef68e3215e79494d56108fecec39cb.svg)

where $\color{blue}x_1$ and ${\color{blue}x_3}$ are basic variables and $\color{red}x_2$ is a free variable. Hence, we obtain that 

![](images/56/56587dc5c1c98493060edb3561c13aa1576187461418619684459dd1f55626fe.svg)

is a basis of $\textrm{Null}(A)$ and, therefore, $\textrm{dim(Null}(A))={\color{red}1}$.

In other words,

$\textrm{dim(Null}(A))$ is equal to the number of *non-pivot* columns in the corresponding row echelon form of $A$

or, equivalently,

$\textrm{dim(Null}(A))$  is the number of *free variables* in the corresponding homogeneous system with the coefficient matrix $A.$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186124684 :activity/expected-seconds 420.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

The answer is yes! The non-pivot columns help to find the dimension of the null space of a matrix $A,$ and here's how.

Consider the matrix 

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix $A$ is already in row echelon form, where the $1$st and the $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd one is a *non-pivot* column. Now, to get the null space of $A,$ we need to find the solution of the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

where $\color{blue}x_1$ and ${\color{blue}x_3}$ are basic variables and $\color{red}x_2$ is a free variable. Hence, we obtain that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3} \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

is a basis of $\textrm{Null}(A)$ and, therefore, $\textrm{dim(Null}(A))={\color{red}1}$.

In other words,

> $\textrm{dim(Null}(A))$ is equal to the number of *non-pivot* columns in the corresponding row echelon form of $A$
